prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core aim: Secure a stronger economy and better public services, rewarding work at every life stage.

Economy and tax
- Eliminate the deficit, then run a surplus in normal times; £30bn further consolidation (departments, welfare, anti-avoidance).
- No rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance; raise Personal Allowance to £12,500 and higher-rate threshold to £50,000; new Tax‑Free Minimum Wage link.
- Crack down on evasion/avoidance; make Office of Tax Simplification permanent.

Growth, infrastructure and regions
- Over £100bn capital investment: HS2/HS3, Crossrail 2, £15bn for roads, real‑terms freeze of regulated rail fares, smart ticketing.
- Broadband to 95% by 2017, ultrafast ambition, 5G leadership; improve mobile coverage.
- Northern Powerhouse and wider devolution to metro mayors; local business rates retention pilots.

Jobs, skills and business
- Aim for full employment and 2m more jobs; 3m new apprenticeships; expand Degree Apprenticeships and UTCs.
- Cut £10bn more red tape; major business rates review; treble Start Up Loans; prompt payment and SME procurement targets.
- Publish gender pay gap data for large firms; halve disability employment gap; invest £6.9bn in research infrastructure and catapults.

Welfare and family
- Roll out Universal Credit; two‑year freeze on working‑age benefits (key exemptions); lower household benefit cap to £23,000.
- 30 hours free childcare for working parents of 3–4 year‑olds; tax‑free childcare up to £2,000/child; support marriage allowance.

Immigration
- Net migration ambition in the tens of thousands; restrict EU migrant access to in‑work benefits for four years; no benefits for jobseekers; tougher deportations and enforcement; English language requirements; Controlling Migration Fund.

Education
- Protect per‑pupil funding; ensure a good primary place; tougher literacy/numeracy standards; EBacc focus; resits for those below standard.
- Convert failing/coasting schools to academies; open 500 new free schools; support teachers and recruit 17,500 extra maths/physics teachers.
- Uncap university places; postgraduate loans; improve FE and employer‑led apprenticeships.

NHS and care
- Increase NHS spending every year; at least £8bn extra by 2020 to deliver the Five Year Forward View.
- 7‑day NHS with 8am–8pm GP access; same‑day GP appointments for over‑75s; parity of esteem for mental health with access standards.
- Cancer Drugs Fund maintained; integrated health and social care; diabetes prevention; electronic health records with opt‑out.

Housing and planning
- Double first‑time buyers; extend Help to Buy; new Help to Buy ISA (25% bonus up to £3,000).
- Build 200,000 Starter Homes (20% discount, under‑40s); 275,000 more affordable homes; extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants with replacements.
- Brownfield first; protect Green Belt; Right to Build.

Energy and environment
- Keep bills low through competition and smart meters by 2020; insulate 1m homes.
- Back nuclear, shale and North Sea; end new subsidies for onshore wind and give locals final say.
- Support Climate Change Act; create a UK/Overseas Territories “Blue Belt”; plant 11m trees; strengthen flood defences; protect animal welfare.

Crime, justice and security
- Complete police reform; tackle cybercrime; ban new psychoactive substances; victims’ law; tougher sentencing where needed; rehabilitation focus.
- Scrap the Human Rights Act; introduce a British Bill of Rights; update communications data powers with oversight.
- Counter‑extremism strategy (banning and disruption orders).

Older people and pensions
- Maintain triple lock; introduce single‑tier pension; preserve pensioner benefits; cap residential care costs and allow deferred payments.
- Raise effective Inheritance Tax threshold on family homes to £1m (couples); pension freedoms and tax‑free inheritance.

Union, EU and world
- English votes for English laws (including tax); implement Smith/St David’s Day; Stormont House in NI.
- Renegotiate EU membership and hold an in/out referendum by end‑2017; keep the pound; protect Single Market; reclaim powers.
- Maintain strong Armed Forces (Army ≥82,000), renew Trident, invest £160bn in equipment; meet 0.7% aid target focused on results.
